_doc: OSCAR Figure 4 (LEFT), Qwen3-8B column: decode throughput speedup vs BF16 at
batch size 1 with a full prefix-cache hit and 1k output length.
Paper Saw-INT4: 1.25 / 1.33 / 1.52 -- NOT implemented in this stack, so that
series is absent rather than substituted by a different baseline.
vq2 is ours and not in the paper; included because 'does vq2 beat OSCAR at
bs=1 long context' is the question this project is asking.
Split-K is pinned per arm: serve_oscar defaults to 48 for vq2 and 8 otherwise,
which would silently compare different schedules. vq2 also gets its tuned 48.

FIDELITY: serving flags follow OSCAR's own rotation/eval_oscar_gpqa.sh -- fa3 prefill, triton decode, --enable-cache-report. Their driver does NOT override --chunked-prefill-size, so sglang's 8192 default applies. Under that config the mixed-KV pool only commits the FIRST prefill chunk to the radix cache (measured cap = chunk - RECENT_TOKENS), so a 100k shared prefix is re-prefilled every request while bf16 caches it fully. chunked_prefill_size=102400 would fix it but OOMs at mem-frac 0.85.
